ORDINANCES

1.. Adoption of General Plan Amendment No. 21-01; Adoption of Specific Plan No. 21-01; Zone Change 21-01; Introduction for First Reading by Title Only an Ordinance  Amending Title 19 (Zoning) of the Commerce Municipal Code to Revise Section 19.05.010 (Zones Established), Adding Section 19.16 (Specific Plans), and Revise Section 19.25.140 (Off-Site Signs Permitted with Restrictions), and an Associated Amendment to the Zoning Map; and a Development Agreement; and Approval of Site Plan No. 997, Master Sign Plan, Vesting Tentative Tract Map No. 83334, and Consider Certifying Environmental Impact Report  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Ivan Altamirano Mayor Mendoza opened Public Hearing. 

Jasmine, and Maria, Commerce residents, opposed the Modelo project and asked that the City Council look into tenant protection policies, anti-harassment policies, and providing more affordable housing in the City of Commerce. 

Andrea Luna opposed the Modelo Project due to the impacts on the community. 

Alfonzo Sanchez, Jose Garcia, Alex Zamora, Richard Licerio, Jason Baiz, Efrain Lopez, Jose Radillo, David Singerman, Jesus Sosa, LiUNA members spoke in support of the Modelo Project. 

Ernesto Pantoja and Ray Morales spoke in support of the Modelo Project and stated that it would bring good-paying jobs to the area. 

Ted Jimenez spoke on behalf of the forty members of Southwest Carpenters Union present in the room, supporting the Modelo Project. This Project would allow local hires and would bring good jobs. 
Juan Serrato, North America Union member, Xiomari, Member of Electrical Union, Brian Jamaine, Jesus Sosa, Union members, Doug Summers, Teamsters Local 70 member, and Albert Duarte, Iron Workers Union member, spoke in support of the Project. Pete, and Omar, Galindo, also union members, spoke in support of the Project. 

Shawn Silva, and Patrick, Creed LA representatives, spoke in support of the Modelo Project and added that this Project would be offering affordable housing elements. 

Gofrey Ashiram, Creed LA representative, also supported the Modelo Project and stated that the smart development calls for density and green space, which this Project would bring to the area. 

Desiree and Edgar Ortiz spoke in support of the Project. 
Mayor Mendoza closed Public Hearing.

The Director of Economic Development and Planning Jimenez, provided a brief introduction and overview. According to Director Jimenez, Creed LA filed an appeal, but it has been withdrawn.

Adrian Comstock provided an overview of the Project, which would include a pedestrian-friendly environment, underground parking, a contemporary Community Center, sports fields, and a museum with rotating exhibitions. 

Patrick Tighe, the Architect for the Modelo Project, stated that this proposed Project evolved over the years. The Modelo development would connect communities. 

Fernando Villa and Marty Akerblom provided an overview of the Final Environmental Impact Report for the Modelo Project. The developer would remediate this property, including Mr.Comstock' property and the City portion of the Modelo Project. In addition, Comstock is making a twelve-million contribution to the Community Center. 

Councilmembers thanked Mr. Comstock and City staff for working hard on this Project of this size. It was a consensus among the City Council that using union labor would also benefit the City and bring good jobs. 
Mr. Comstock partnered with labor and provided jobs locally. Further discussion took place that initially it was proposed as a warehouse, but since the City Council is looking into bringing more housing, this Project evolved into the Modelo project that also offers affordable housing. 

Mayor Mendoza added that this would be a great neighborhood that everyone could enjoy since it would have a grocery store, community center, and sports fields. In addition, this property would be remediated. This Project would provide jobs to local union members, and people would be able to rent or purchase townhouses or condos. In addition, traffic in the area would improve from grade D to grade B by improving this area. 






2.. First Reading of Uncodified Ordinance Approving Amended and Restated Development Agreement Related to Application #18-074 and Replacing Commercial Cannabis Development Agreements No. 724  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Oralia Rebollo Knarik Vizcarra, Contract Planner, provided and overview of the staff report.
